author: Astra
scope: Product specification corrections only; no source, tests, dependencies, root copies, installed CLI, or external systems changed.

findings.evidence: Original P2 allowed a private state location and S1 referred to resolved scheduler configuration without a canonical identity; neither described nested ptest under the required ptest test harness. AGENTS.md mandates test execution through ptest, so budget-1 parent/child waiting is a real missing contract.
findings.change: P2/S1 now fix the normal root/domain by host and OS account rather than per-invocation environment. Same-domain nested executing invocations return 75/nested-invocation before queueing, with live ancestry validation. A sole explicit private fixture-domain mechanism is labeled isolated, cannot activate from repo/env settings, uses bounded synthetic or miniature isolated workloads within the outer allowance, and cannot publish normal history/baselines. A2/A4 require domain/nesting/fixture negative cases.
findings.disputed_premise_or_fix: Do not add a general production alternate-domain override: it would expand scope and weaken same-user coordination. The explicit alternative is limited to controlled fixture validation; state relocation and nested reservation lending are deferred.

findings.evidence: Original T3 required no baseline/full-gate evidence after relevant changes but stated no process exit status. Original C3 permitted nonzero operational status for invalid full-gate evidence. Thus the claimed T3 exit-0 promise was not present; the actual gap was optional wording and undefined input/output classification.
findings.change: T3, fallback table, and C3 now require incomplete/changed-during-run, full_gate_eligible=false, and final 70 when automatic/full runner_exit_code is 0. Actual nonzero runner status is preserved. Declared coverage/report/cache outputs are exempt only if they do not supply selection, configuration, assertions, or runtime inputs. Source, tracked snapshots/goldens, generated inputs, ambiguous overlaps, and requested expectation updates remain relevant; final inputs need a subsequent unchanged gate. A5/A11 cover both safe output writes and invalidating edits. Coverage-only failures are explicit unresolved full-gate obligations.
findings.disputed_premise_or_fix: Rejected recommended exit 0 for an invalidated full gate because shell-only consumers would infer false verification. Rejected exemption of snapshot updates merely because the runner requested/owns them; changed expectations need re-verification. T3 ambiguity was corrected without claiming it previously required exit 0.

findings.evidence: Original Exposure/C1 promised that arbitrary secret argv values would not leak while requiring effective-command inspection, without defining a display policy. Unknown names, positional values, URLs, and option-looking secrets cannot all be recognized by a finite secret-name list.
findings.change: C1 separates literal execution from display. Defaults expose only a validated command summary and withhold arbitrary configured/caller argv strings, including executable paths and option-looking tokens; parsing errors use the same policy. Explicit local command reveal in where/init preview is labeled unredacted, never retained as argv history, and never dumps environment values. Exposure/A8/A11 now specify exact omission fixtures and explicitly retain OS process listings, raw runner streams, arbitrary test/path names, and intentional reveal as residual exposure surfaces.
findings.disputed_premise_or_fix: Did not adopt a deny-list as universal sanitization. Default omission of arbitrary argv is testable without guessing secret names; intentional reveal is explicitly outside that guarantee.

notes.evidence: Legacy ptest default_commands and main autodetect unregistered repos; main rejects bare/root-scoped runs; README states status exits 1 for attention. resolve_project reads also_roots and cmd_register prints a machine stanza.
notes.change: P2/P4/A1 explicitly require init before execution, preserve static pre-init diagnostics, enumerate bare/root/status/register changes, and migrate also_roots as independently adopted configs.

notes.evidence: The original S4 named behavior but not signal triggers, and no cancel command was in the required surface.
notes.change: S4/A3 name SIGINT/SIGTERM including TUI process-group delivery. Parent-only SIGKILL leaves live work charged with ownership-checked manual guidance; a cancel/reclaim command is explicitly deferred.

notes.evidence: Legacy main resolves git_root(cwd) or cwd and passes it to run_local, explicitly avoiding the original source checkout when in a worktree.
notes.change: C1/A11 state child cwd is the current resolved project root in the active checkout, with root-relative argv and no silent path rebasing.

notes.evidence: The original spec required a generic guide and pointer snippets without stating how the target exists before optional repo export.
notes.change: CLI/section 9/A13 define bundled ptest guide output before init, optional non-overwriting docs/ptest-agent.md export/recipe, and pointers only to an existing file or the stable command. Plain init does not add guide or native entry files.

notes.evidence: The specified config had a single runner and nearest-project resolution, but root-level multi-runner behavior was unstated.
notes.change: P2/A1 explicitly use one runner per project config and separate nested roots; ambiguous root commands fail rather than choosing one, and a project's full gate is not an aggregate monorepo gate.

notes.topic: Doctor inspection priority and higher budgets
notes.evidence: The original fixed default bounds did not say whether relevant setup/tests received priority or could be inspected with a larger explicitly bounded request.
notes.change: D1/A8 prioritize declared test/setup/fixture/config roots deterministically, report traversal-discovery limits honestly, and allow explicit finite higher budgets/narrower scope within design-frozen upper bounds. Unlimited scans remain unsupported.

notes.evidence: The reviewer labeled this a preference. An arbitrary wrapper has no verified inner concurrency control in the v1 support tier.
notes.change: Retain the exclusive whole-capacity reservation and best-effort label. User-attested smaller reservations are deferred until supported by a separate bounded adapter/resource contract; they are not necessary to resolve F1-F3.

notes.evidence: T3 already required a successful complete full gate; coverage failure therefore cannot provide a baseline, but the effect on existing selection evidence was not explicit.
notes.change: T3/T4/A5 state coverage failure cannot seed a baseline and remains a full-gate obligation forcing full until a complete successful gate, even if an older valid dependency baseline exists.

notes.evidence: Legacy code registers and caps local invocations but does not implement NG's canonical shared admission domain.
notes.change: P4/A1 document that side-by-side binaries do not share a budget, legacy work must be stopped/drained before relying on the NG ceiling, and neither jobs nor the live CLI are automatically replaced.

notes.evidence: The reviewer confirmed the cited legacy paths and compatibility research claims; no correction was requested by this note.
notes.change: Retained existing provenance and the narrow Muse loading-smoke qualification. No new native integration claims or provider calls.

checks: JSON parsing and expected F1-F3/N1-N10 disposition keys
validation.runtime_claims: None: acceptance and negative cases are requirements for later implementation, not executed tests.

remaining_decisions: Linux+macOS remains the proposed v1 target pending the user's platform preference.
User approval of the reviewed spec remains mandatory before detailed design.
License choice and publication/live-install approval remain separate release gates.
